blocks.task_summary: State the equation of the vertical asymptote to the graph of y = g(x) = 2ln x − ln d.
method_path: Recognise ln x has vertical asymptote at x = 0

evidence.basis: Markscheme entry: '0 = x A1' awarding 1 mark for the asymptote x = 0.

blocks.task_summary: Given f(x)=ln(2x−9) and g(x)=2ln x−ln d intersect at two distinct points: (i) show x²−2dx+9d=0, (ii) hence show d²−9d>0, (iii) find the range of possible values of d.
method_path: Apply quotient rule to obtain ln(2x−9)=ln(x²/d) or equivalent
Require Δ>0 for two distinct real roots
Solve with constraint d∈ℝ⁺ to obtain d>9
accepted_alternatives: Log form ln(x²/(2x−9))=ln d leading to x²/(2x−9)=d
Inequality solved by d(d−9)=0, sketch graph, sign test, or d²>9d

evidence.basis: Part (b)(i): M1 for setting ln(2x−9)=2ln x−ln d; (M1) for power rule; (M1) for product/quotient rule; A1 for correct logarithmic equation leading to AG x²−2dx+9d=0. Part (b)(ii): (A1) for discriminant expression; (M1) for recognising discriminant>0; A1 for correct inequality leading to AG d²−9d>0. Part (b)(iii): (M1) for solving d(d−9)>0 by factorisation, sketch, sign test or equivalent; A1 for d>9.

blocks.task_summary: When d=10, find q−p where the graphs intersect at x=p and x=q (p<q), expressing the answer in the form a√b with a,b∈ℤ⁺.
method_path: Substitute d=10 into x²−2dx+9d=0 to get x²−20x+90=0

evidence.basis: A1 for x²−20x+90=0; (M1) for attempting to solve the quadratic; (A1) for x=10−√10=p and x=10+√10=q; (M1) for subtracting their values of x; A1 for distance=2√10. Note accepts 1√40 or √40.
